t: An island sultanate off southern Tanzania that grew rich as the middleman between the gold of the Zimbabwe plateau and the Indian Ocean.
Its Great Mosque, the palace of Husuni Kubwa and its copper coinage made Kilwa a showpiece of medieval Swahili culture.
Factional strife weakened it in the 15th century, and the Portuguese sack of 1505 ended its power on the coast.
dyk: In 1944 five copper coins from Kilwa were found on Marchinbar Island off northern Australia, thousands of kilometres from East Africa; how they got there is still unknown.
ev: Traditional date for the founding of the dynasty by Ali ibn al-Hasan of Shiraz
The Mahdali dynasty, of Yemeni origin, seizes power in Kilwa
Al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman becomes sultan and begins the palace of Husuni Kubwa
Ibn Battuta visits Kilwa and praises the generosity of its sultan
Vasco da Gama forces Emir Ibrahim to pay tribute to Portugal
Francisco de Almeida sacks Kilwa and builds Fort Santiago
The Portuguese withdraw their garrison from Kilwa
The ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara become a UNESCO World Heritage Site

f.successor: Portuguese overlordship; later Omani rule and the Sultanate of Zanzibar
